title: Vectory protocol v1
description: Validate one named schema via $defs. Cryptographic, authorization and semantic checks remain mandatory.

oneOf.description: Server also limits UTF-8 encoding to 4096 bytes.

defaults.description: Values must exactly match published declaration names and types. Missing, extra, and secret-like values are rejected by the server.

oneOf.description: Server also limits UTF-8 encoding to 4096 bytes.

additionalProperties.description: Values must exactly match published declaration names and types. Missing, extra, and secret-like values are rejected by the server.

message.description: Agent requests may send any bounded text; server responses replace it with a reason rendered from the code and first diagnostic (at most 500 characters).

diagnostics.description: Structured findings the agent or the server reports about a device, errors first, at most 10.

device_name.description: The current name of device_id, or null when no device exists with that ID.
The current name of device_id, or null when no device exists with that ID.

scope.description: changes hides sign-in and sign-out activity (login, login.*, logout); security shows only sign-in, account, user, MFA, bootstrap and signing-key events. Omitted means every event.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. Common: UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, STALE_REVISION, INVALID_INPUT, RATE_LIMITED, SIGNIN_THROTTLED, CAPACITY_BUSY (agent listener or download slots busy, or a membership preview found the writer busy; retry after Retry-After), REQUEST_TIMEOUT (agent request deadline), PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (body over its limit), EXPORT_BUSY, EXPORT_CAPACITY, EXPORT_STORAGE, EXPORT_TIMEOUT, EXPORT_TOO_LARGE, VALIDATION_FAILED, TESTS_FAILED, INTERNAL. CONTRACT.md lists every code.

reason.description: GET /session 401 only: why this browser's session ended (expired, signed_out, signed_out_elsewhere, password_changed, access_changed, mfa_changed, mfa_reset, replaced, revoked) or null.

details.description: Additive. Present on a 409 CONFLICT that refuses a group edit for conflicting equal-priority assignments (PUT /groups/{id}, POST /groups) and on the matching blocker of a membership preview: at most the first ten collisions, ordered by device name, then device ID. Absent on every other error; older clients ignore it.

details_total.description: How many collisions the edit creates in all; details lists at most ten of them.

AccessEditRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped exact-target access edit status. An applied user is the immutable public commit snapshot, not necessarily the account’s current state. not_found is noncausal while a PUT may be in flight; cancellation fences only an absent request and cannot undo an applied edit.

Person.description: Administrator view of one account. invited means no password has been chosen yet; invite_expires_at is the live invitation expiry, if any.

UserRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped, secret-free current status. not_found is not cancellation: an in-flight POST may still commit. A repeated keyed POST always conflicts; cancel fences a late create only when it wins the writer transaction.

ResetRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped, exact-target, secret-free reset issuance status. A negative read does not fence an in-flight POST. Issued active is true only while this exact code verifier remains current and unexpired for an enabled account. Cancellation revokes the exact still-current unused code and fences late issuance; it cannot undo a code already redeemed.

config.description: Canonical Vector configuration; unknown properties are preserved. Secrets and unsafe capabilities are validated independently.

variables.description: Draft-owned nonsecret scalar replacement slots, captured immutably in each published version. Paths are canonical RFC6901 pointers to existing leaves; server validation rejects structural and known credential fields and rechecks each rendered configuration against target capabilities.

archived.description: Organization/editing state only. Archived drafts cannot be saved, restored or published; all immutable versions remain readable and deployable.

PipelineRequestLookup.description: Nested request_id must equal the outer key. A duplicate result UUID must differ from its source. Current result contents may have changed since creation; original operation/source metadata remains immutable.

running_versions.description: Non-revoked devices grouped by the version of this pipeline they last verified, highest number first

detail.description: Plain text of the Vector compiler block for this finding, derived from the checked draft.

scope.description: span replaces length characters at line:column; line replaces the whole line.

message.description: Reason rendered on read from the code and the first error diagnostic; stored free text is never shown.

diagnostics.description: Structured findings the agent or the server reports about a device, errors first, at most 10.

count.description: Distinct failed attempts (a new desired generation or local materialization), not check-ins.

reports.description: Every failure report, including repeated check-ins about the same attempt.

anyOf.description: verified: a configuration verified after an apply failure. unassigned: the assignment was removed. healthy: a DATA_PLANE_* condition was clear for three evaluations. superseded: the device no longer runs the version a DATA_PLANE_* issue was measured on. unmonitored: the device's settings turned metrics off, so delivery can no longer be judged. revoked: the device identity was revoked (by an operator or an identity recovery), so it can never report again.

diagnostics.description: Structured findings the agent or the server reports about a device, errors first, at most 10.

devices.description: Every device as GET /api/v1/devices lists it. Omitted with slim=1.

devices_managed.description: Non-revoked devices with a desired version.

devices_on_desired.description: Managed devices verified on their desired version (status verified).

devices_degraded.description: Of those, devices with an open DATA_PLANE_* issue on that version.

versions.description: Pipeline name and number for each desired version referenced by a device.

rollouts.description: Active and paused rollouts (newest first), then scheduled ones starting within 24 hours (soonest first).

attention.description: Devices needing an operator, grouped by cause and ordered by severity.

fleet_activity.description: Recent fleet-changing events; sign-in, account and signing-key events are excluded.

security_events_hidden.description: Security events skipped within the scanned window (at most 300 recent events).

devices_offline_on_desired.description: Additive; absent from older servers. Managed devices that are offline and whose last verified version is the one they are assigned: out of reach right now, not unverified. Never part of devices_on_desired, which counts only devices verified now.

offline_on_desired_version.description: Additive; absent from older servers. The number of the one version the devices counted in devices_offline_on_desired last verified, when they share one; null when there are none or they differ.

devices_unmeasured.description: Applied devices (status verified) with no metrics sample in the last three minutes: their delivery cannot be measured.

attention_devices.description: Devices that need a person, most urgent first.

busiest.description: Live devices by fresh events in per second, busiest first.

running.description: What runs where, most devices first, then by pipeline name.

degraded.description: Devices that applied this version but are not delivering it: verified_applied targets with an open data-plane issue measured on it. The rollout lanes count them as failed; state_counts keeps their recorded state.

cause.description: degraded: verified on the desired version, with an open DATA_PLANE_* issue measured on it. held: the desired version failed, but the device verifiably keeps running an earlier one and delivers on it (severity warning; failed keeps the devices that have no working version).

anyOf.description: Most common sanitized failure summary reported for failed groups.

requested.description: Paused groups only: pauses not yet acknowledged by the agent.

local.description: Paused groups only: pauses set on the host.

adopted.description: Unmanaged groups only: devices running a local configuration adopted at setup (Vector not reported stopped).

title.description: Degraded groups only: the most common leading data-plane issue title.

fix.description: Degraded groups only: that issue's fix.

code.description: Degraded groups only: that issue's DATA_PLANE_* code.

component_id.description: Degraded groups only: the component it names, if any.

deployment_id.description: Failed and degraded groups: the deployment every device in the group is assigned, when they share one; null otherwise.

rollback_available.description: Failed and degraded groups: that deployment is a configuration rollout the server can review for rollback now (not rolled back, a candidate status, and a released current target with a previously managed version). False otherwise.

repeat.description: Consecutive per-device events collapsed into this row.

rolled_back_to_configuration_name.description: For a rolled-back deployment: the pipeline its rollback restored.

rolled_back_to_version_number.description: For a rolled-back deployment: the version its rollback restored.

rolled_back_device_count.description: For a rolled-back deployment: the devices its rollback targets.

rollback_of_configuration_name.description: For a rollback deployment: the pipeline of the deployment it rolled back.

rollback_of_version_number.description: For a rollback deployment: the version it rolled back.

FleetActivity.description: deployment.rollback rows name the rolled-back deployment (target) and carry device_names: up to five devices its rollback returned, by name.

name.description: Nonempty, at most 120 UTF-8 bytes, with no NUL character. The byte bound is enforced by the server and dashboard.

PolicyRequestLookup.description: The outer request identity must match the nested receipt and the expected actor-scoped request. A negative read does not prove an in-flight request cannot still commit.

canary_device_ids.description: Canary rollouts only: the devices to release first. Distinct lowercase device UUIDs, at most canary_size and at most 100, each a device the request targets (otherwise 400 INVALID_INPUT on preview and create). Fewer than canary_size: the most ready of the remaining targets fill the canary. Absent, null or empty: the scheduler chooses, online and healthy devices that report metrics first and device ID order among equals.

sent_by_output.description: Events per second sent on each named output (route/remap outputs); `_default` is the unnamed output.

items.description: One component in the latest sample. events_per_second is the sent rate. errors and discarded_* are cumulative counters since Vector started; *_per_minute and *_per_second are rates over the agent sampling window. discarded_intentional counts filter/sample drops (expected); discarded_error counts drops caused by errors. Missing values are unavailable, never zero.

configuration_mode.description: Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.

status.description: Computed status. awaiting_first_check_in: enrolled but never checked in. offline: more than three check-in intervals late.

labels.description: Descriptive labels from the enrollment token that enrolled the device (at most 8; lowercase keys, values of 1 to 128 characters without control characters). They never grant group membership, assignments, policy or secret access.

retry_preconditions.description: Retry requires the reviewed desired version and generation plus current retryable state and enabled sync.

desired_sha256.description: Exact rendered artifact digest for the currently released device generation. Version identity, delivered artifact bytes, and actual managed-file digest are distinct.

reported_apply_state.description: Agent-reported workload state, separate from progress of the current desired assignment.

vector_log_summary.description: Latest summary from an agent that reports it; absent for agents that do not.

evaluations.description: Evaluations on this version, counted up to the canary measurement count (3 by default; editable under Settings → Notifications → Detection, 1 to 20).

issue_count.description: Open issues on this version. List rows (DeviceListItem) carry only the first of them in issues.

data_plane.description: Data-plane health measured from telemetry on the version the device verifiably runs, or, when the device reports no metrics, from sink request failures in its Vector log summary (weaker evidence; evaluations stays 0); absent until the first evaluation. The device reads Not delivering while status is verified, version_id equals desired_version_id and issues is nonempty.

held_on_previous_version.description: Present only, and true, on a device whose status is failed or rolled_back but which verifiably keeps running an earlier version (its managed file still matches the digest the agent verified for it), whose Vector is not reported stopped, and which has no open delivery issue measured on that version. It is held there, not failed: status stays what the agent reported. Absent otherwise, and on older servers.

secret_names.description: Secret names bound on the device, sorted, as its agent last reported them; absent for agents that do not report them. A version needs the names of its vectory-secret:NAME references.

service_manager.description: What keeps the agent running, from enrollment and the latest check-in that reported it; absent for agents that do not report it. none means no service manager keeps it running: after setup's single check-in nothing does until the operator runs it.

vector_running.description: Whether Vector runs on the device, from its latest check-in; absent when the agent does not report it. false with a failed first version means nothing runs.

agent_features.description: What the agent announced it can do in its latest check-in (validation: it can be checked on, see Check on devices); absent when that check-in announced nothing. Names the server does not know are kept as given and never acted on.

readiness.description: Facts the agent reported about the host in its latest check-in: whether its data directory is writable and how many listeners its local capability policy allows (a count, never the list). Absent when that check-in reported none; each member is absent when the agent did not say. Reported, not verified by the server.

agent_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the agent build running on the device, from its latest check-in; absent when the agent does not report it. Compared with the release catalog to say a device already runs a build.

state_dir.description: Where the agent keeps its state on the device, from its latest check-in; absent when the agent does not report it. The deploy dialog puts it in the host commands it writes.

check_in_seconds.description: Current check-in interval; until the agent acknowledges a policy change, the longer of the old and new interval.

running_version.description: Last verified managed version on the host, which keeps running after a failed update or a removed assignment. Null means no managed version was ever verified (the host runs its adopted local config).

listening.description: The device's agent holds a wait (GET /agent/v1/wait) at this instant, so a change usually reaches it within seconds (a large release is paced, never past the device's next check-in). False between waits, for agents with wake-ups off or without them, and for offline devices. Never evidence that anything was delivered or applied.

wake.description: GET /api/v1/devices/{id} only, while the server offers wake-ups (absent when VECTORY_AGENT_WAKE_LIMIT=0). Read-only, from the in-memory wait registry.

groups.description: Only with include=groups: the groups this device belongs to, by name (at most 100), and how many.

rollback_idempotency.description: This server supports durable actor-scoped rollback request identities.

rollback_review.description: This server supports read-only rollback scope review and a transactionally checked review token.

request_correlation.description: Keyed create/rollback receipts and exact request lookup echo durable request, operation and source identity.

rollback_idempotency.description: This server supports durable actor-scoped rollback request identities.

rollback_review.description: This server supports read-only rollback scope review and a transactionally checked review token.

request_correlation.description: Keyed create/rollback receipts and exact request lookup echo durable request, operation and source identity.

canary_gate.description: Present only on the single-deployment summary for active/paused canaries; omitted from paged history and other rollout states. Absence does not establish readiness.

rollback_available.description: Some released current target recorded a previously managed version.

rolled_back_to_configuration_name.description: The pipeline the rollback restored, which may differ from this deployment's own.

rollback_of_configuration_name.description: The pipeline of the deployment this one rolled back.

rollback.description: The replaced assignment is itself a rollback, so it runs the version it restored.

degraded.description: Devices that applied this version but are not delivering it: verified_applied targets with an open data-plane issue measured on it. The rollout lanes count them as failed; state_counts keeps their recorded state.

DeploymentSummary.description: Status is the assignment lifecycle. status_before_removal and status_before_rollback keep how the rollout itself ended when an assignment is later removed, replaced or rolled back.

request_history.description: Supporting servers offer authenticated actor-scoped committed deployment request discovery.

gate_reason.description: Current gate blocker for this target of an active/paused canary. Null also covers pending or no-longer-targeted rows and must not be interpreted as verified. Omitted outside this context or by older servers.

delivery.description: Present only on a verified_applied row whose device has an open data-plane issue on the deployment's version: the issue's title, measured reason and fix. The recorded state is unchanged.

replaced_by.description: For a removed row: the deployment that replaced this assignment on the device.

diagnostic.description: First sanitized diagnostic the agent reported for this exact candidate, when available.

failure_stage.description: Apply stage the agent reported for this exact candidate's failure (for example validation, reload or rollback), when available. Omitted by older servers.

check_in_seconds.description: Longest interval the agent may currently take between check-ins.

timeline.description: Recorded apply-state changes after release, oldest first. Heartbeats can skip states.

listening.description: The device's agent holds a wait (GET /agent/v1/wait) at this instant, so a change usually reaches it within seconds (a large release is paced, never past the device's next check-in). False between waits, for agents with wake-ups off or without them, and for offline devices. Never evidence that anything was delivered or applied.

wake.description: Target pages only, while the server offers wake-ups: the same projection as Device wake, for this row's device.

request_id.description: Optional durable create identity scoped to the authenticated actor. Reuse only with the identical payload.

name.description: Optional; at most 120 characters. No line breaks, control characters or text-direction overrides, at the ends too: a name that has one is refused with 400 and a sentence that names the field.

replaces.description: Existing assignments of the same resource that this deployment explicitly replaces on the selected devices. Until this deployment releases a device the replaced assignment keeps it; each release retires the replaced assignment there (history kept, persistent selectors exclude the device). An assignment left with nothing to deliver is retired (status unassigned, status_before_removal kept). Without replaces, equal-priority different payloads still conflict. A replaced assignment that changed or no longer selects any of these devices returns 409 REPLACEMENT_CHANGED.

policy_id.description: Saved agent settings a policy deployment applies. The policy must equal their current values, otherwise preview and creation return 409.

DeploymentReceipt.description: Current original result with response-only durable request identity. For rollback, result ID differs from source ID. Mutable deployment state and targets need not equal the original request.

DeploymentRequestStatus.description: Outer request_id, operation and source_deployment_id must exactly match the nested receipt and the locally frozen operation. A negative read is not proof an in-flight request failed.

outcome.description: replace: the device moves from the listed replaced assignment when this deployment releases it.

winner.description: The assignment that currently wins for this device and resource, possibly not yet released.

replaces.description: The requested replacement that covers this device.

request_correlation.description: Keyed create/rollback receipts and exact request lookup echo durable request, operation and source identity.

replacements.description: The effect of the requested replaces list. retires_assignment is true when nothing is left for the replaced assignment to deliver, including future members of a persistent selector.

suggested_replaces.description: Current winners of the same pipeline (or any agent settings) with a different payload, which a reviewed deployment would normally replace, plus every assignment of the pipeline's lineage that still binds a reviewed device at or above the requested priority: its own cancelled or rolled-back deployments and their rollbacks (rollback_of chains).

replacements_needed.description: Every existing assignment, at any priority at or above the request, whose different payload keeps a reviewed device from taking it (conflict or higher_priority outcomes). Replacing all of them resolves the review in one step. Omitted by older servers.

suggested_priority.description: Highest priority among suggested replacements, to reuse.

configuration_name.description: Current name of the pipeline whose version is previewed; null for agent settings. Omitted by older servers.

winning_priority.description: Lowest priority that would outrank every existing winner on conflicting or outranked devices, when one exists.

canary.description: Canary rollouts only, null otherwise. A chosen device that is not checking in, paused or failing adds a warning: the rollout waits for it. Omitted by older servers.

paused_device_ids.description: Configuration targets whose sync is paused; they apply the change after sync resumes.

validation_id.description: Present when device_validation was requested and at least one device was addressed: read the answers with GET /api/v1/device-validations/{id}. Nothing was deployed.

validation_truncated.description: Present with validation_id: true when more devices were reviewed than were addressed (the first 50 by name, and at most 10 MiB of candidate bytes in all).

member_count.description: Number of device_ids; group lists (GET /api/v1/groups) only.

device_name.description: Enrolls only this device name (normalized to lowercase). Absent: any unique name.

allowed_names.description: Normalized preapproved device names. Only a device whose normalized name is listed can enroll, each name once. Present only on tokens created with a list.

labels.description: Descriptive labels from the enrollment token that enrolled the device (at most 8; lowercase keys, values of 1 to 128 characters without control characters). They never grant group membership, assignments, policy or secret access.

enrolled_names.description: Token list only: preapproved names that already enrolled.

created_by.description: Token list only: the account that created it (recovery: authorized it).

last_used_at.description: Token list only: when it last enrolled a device.

device_count.description: Token list only: devices it enrolled.

devices.description: Token list only: most recently enrolled devices.

device_name.description: Enrolls only this device name (normalized to lowercase). Absent: any unique name.

allowed_names.description: Normalized preapproved device names. Only a device whose normalized name is listed can enroll, each name once. Present only on tokens created with a list.

labels.description: Descriptive labels from the enrollment token that enrolled the device (at most 8; lowercase keys, values of 1 to 128 characters without control characters). They never grant group membership, assignments, policy or secret access.

TokenRequestStatus.description: Actor-scoped exact creation identity. Lookup never reveals a secret. A negative read is not cancellation; cancellation fences late creation and revokes the mapped token atomically.

DeviceRecoveryRequestStatus.description: Current administrator own recovery request bound to its original device UUID. Record recovery_device_id must equal envelope device_id, and recovery_name must equal the reviewed expected_name. No secret replay. A negative read does not fence late issuance. Cancellation revokes only the mapped token; completed replacement identities remain unchanged.

DeviceRecoveryRequest.description: Empty legacy request or strict correlated request. The expected name must exactly match the original source device on first issuance. Same actor/request key cannot be rebound to another device or reviewed name.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the CA certificate DER: the fingerprint operators compare and the issuer recorded on each device credential.

devices.description: Active devices that still hold an unexpired, unrevoked certificate from this CA (including credentials issued before issuers were recorded). Retiring waits for zero.

device_names.description: Up to 20 of those devices by name.

last_expires_at.description: When the last of those certificates expires: retiring succeeds by then at the latest.

schedule_late_start_seconds.description: How late a scheduled deployment still activates once (VECTORY_SCHEDULE_LATE_START_SECONDS); later ones become missed.

previous.description: The CA a rotation replaced, still trusted for client certificates until vectory-admin retire-device-ca; null when none.

ca_pem.description: The CA certificate itself (PEM), public like its fingerprint. Add device writes it on the host so the command that fetches the installer verifies the server against it.

catalog_problems.description: Why catalog entries are not offered; administrators only, empty for other roles.

source.description: bundled with the server image, or from the operator mirror, which replaces a platform bundled build

static_checked.description: The isolated worker ran pinned Vector on this draft (with placeholders and stand-ins where only a device can resolve a value).

deferred.description: Each device still checks environment, secrets, files or platform before applying.

placeholders.description: Secret and environment references that were replaced by typed placeholders for the static check.

not_run.description: True when Vector did not run this test, for example because another test could not be read or built. Such a test never passes.

refused.description: True when Vector could not read or build this test, so it never ran. Its message says why.

outputs.description: Output payloads Vector printed for a failed test, from the draft's synthetic test inputs.

tests.description: One row per configured test, not_run rows included. Each detail is cut to 1,000 characters and outputs are left out; POST /configurations/test returns the full rows.

tests_run.description: Vector ran the tests, so each row is its verdict. False when no runner answered.

failed.description: Vector ran the test and it failed.

refused.description: Vector could not read or build the test.

not_run.description: Vector did not run the test.

port.description: Named output, or an empty string for the default output.

timestamps.description: Flattened field paths whose values are timestamps.

configuration_mode.description: Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.

service_manager.description: What setup registered to keep the agent running. Optional: servers that predate it ignore it, and a value this server does not know is ignored.

configuration_mode.description: Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.

diagnostics.description: Structured findings the agent or the server reports about a device, errors first, at most 10.

vector_log_summary.description: Sent only to servers that list the feature; an empty list means nothing to report.

secret_names.description: Names bound with vectory configure-secrets: names only, never file paths or values. Sent only to servers that list the secret_names feature; an empty list means the host binds none.

service_manager.description: What keeps this agent process running: the service manager it runs under, or none (a foreground run, a supervisor of the operator's own, or setup's one-shot check-in). Sent only to servers that list the service_manager feature.

vector_running.description: Whether the Vector process the agent supervises is running. Sent only to servers that list the vector_running feature.

agent_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the running agent executable. Sent only to servers that list the agent_sha256 feature.

state_dir.description: The agent state directory, an absolute local path (POSIX, or a Windows drive path) and not a secret. Sent only to servers that list the state_dir feature.

agent_features.description: What this agent can do: validation means it can be checked on. Sent only after a verified manifest lists validation. The server keeps the latest announcement per device; a check-in without it means nothing is announced now. Null is treated as absent.

validation_result.description: The answer to the check the manifest carried. Null is treated as absent.

readiness.description: Booleans and counts only (data_dir_writable, allowed_listener_count), sent only after a verified manifest lists validation. configuration_mode and vector_version already ride every heartbeat. Null is treated as absent, here and for each member.

sha256.description: Digest of exact target-specific rendered artifact bytes, not necessarily the published base-version digest.

version_number.description: Optional, for vectory status: the number of version_id within its pipeline. Covered by the signature like the rest; omitted when the server does not know it. An older agent ignores it. Not part of the desired identity: it never changes for a version_id.

configuration_name.description: Optional, for vectory status: the pipeline's name as the server shows it now (cut to 120 characters, omitted when it is empty or has a control character, a line or paragraph separator or a text-direction control). It can change at an unchanged generation when the pipeline is renamed, so an agent must keep it out of the identity it compares for a repeated generation. An older agent ignores it.

features.description: Additive heartbeat fields this server accepts (diagnostics, host_runtime, vector_log_summary, telemetry_v2, secret_names, service_manager, vector_running, agent_sha256, state_dir), validation (agent_features, validation_result and readiness, see Check on devices), and wake while it holds GET /agent/v1/wait. Agents send those fields, and wait, only when listed, so older servers keep their strict validation. Unknown names are ignored.

validation.description: At most one, optional: the device check this device is asked to run now. Present only while the device has an unexpired, unanswered check and announced agent_features:["validation"] in the heartbeat this manifest answers. Covered by the signature and bound to the recipient and nonce like every other member. An agent ignores it when expires_at is in the past or later than 15 minutes after issued_at.

payload.description: Exact UTF-8 JSON Manifest bytes, decoded before signature verification

signature.description: Ed25519 signature over exact decoded payload

HostRuntime.description: What the host contributes beyond the signed artifact. data_dir_source: pipeline (the configuration sets data_dir), host (install --vector-data-dir), adopted (the adopted configuration's data_dir), vector_default (Vector's own default exists and is writable), agent_default (a private directory the agent created). The host value reaches Vector through a separate runtime file, so the managed artifact digest is unchanged. metrics_source: explicit (local metrics URL), discovered (a loopback prometheus_exporter sink in the running configuration) or none. activation: how the last change was activated (reload via SIGHUP with verified completion, or restart).

VectorLogGroup.description: Recent Vector WARN/ERROR log lines grouped by a fingerprint of component and normalized message. Messages are redacted like diagnostics. Counts are since the agent started.

CanaryGate.description: Read-only current canary evidence, separate from historical progress. Each released target contributes exactly once to verified_count or one reason. Only observing has a nonnull observation start and requires every released target to be currently verified. Counts and evaluation share a read snapshot; no countdown or future release promise.

artifact_sha256.description: Null when the device had no previously managed version before this deployment; the preview is then blocked with PRIOR_VERSION_UNKNOWN.

effect.description: What the device is set to run once the rollback stops the rollout: unchanged (it keeps it), retained_pending (it keeps it until another rollout releases it, see next), fallback (it would switch to next; blocks with UNSAFE_SOURCE_REMOVAL) or unmanaged (it would lose its pipeline; blocks). Null for revoked or missing devices, or when current assignments conflict.

current.description: The version the device is set to run now.

next.description: fallback: the version it would switch to; retained_pending: the version of the rollout still waiting to release it.

RollbackPreview.description: Complete metadata-only historical scope, bounded to 10000 distinct device UUIDs across both lists. Ready requires at least one eligible device, a common previous version and no blockers. Each eligible target exposes the exact prior artifact digest, never its bytes or binding values. Names are display-only. Confirming stops the rollout (cancelled, or unassigned at the priority ceiling) in the same transaction; each excluded device states what it runs afterwards, simulated with the real resolver, and only one that would switch to an unreviewed version or lose its pipeline blocks, by name. The token binds source, exact eligible/excluded identities and reasons, prior version, prior target artifact digests and generations, admission, current assignment state and what each excluded device runs once the rollout stops.

AssignmentRemovalPreview.description: Read-only removal simulation. Every device identity is distinct, ready is true exactly when blockers is empty, and an empty ready scope is allowed. Fingerprint binds the actor, source and meaningful current/projected delivery state, not display metadata or telemetry. Configuration removal can retain local workload; policy removal can restore defaults. Pending candidates are not delivered assignments.

resource.description: Compatibility blockers only: the resource the schedule releases.

device_ids.description: Compatibility blockers only (FULL_VECTOR_MODE_REQUIRED, VECTOR_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE): the proposed devices the blocker affects, each once. Other blockers speak for the whole schedule and omit it.

ScheduledRefreshPreview.description: Read-only comparison of the saved scheduled snapshot and current selector resolution. Device identities are distinct within each list; the combined union is bounded to10000. Ready is true exactly when blockers is empty; an empty proposed selection is blocked. New UUIDs without complete typed bindings produce VARIABLE_BINDING_REQUIRED; the actor-bound token covers frozen bindings, source settings, saved/proposed membership and an internal monotonic revision so delayed requests cannot overwrite a newer review, including an ABA change. Matching no-op does not mutate or audit. Names and connection status are display metadata. Current saved selection does not attribute an earlier request or establish activation.

coverage.description: Number of fresh device samples that reported each total. Compare with devices_reporting to state partial coverage.

TelemetrySummary.description: Fleet totals from each non-revoked device's latest sample when it is fresh (at most max(180 s, three check-ins) old), plus a downsampled series (per-device mean within each step, summed across devices). A total no fresh device reported is null, never zero.

device_ids.description: Devices whose fresh samples are included.

coverage.description: Number of fresh device samples that reported each total. Compare with devices_reporting to state partial coverage.

anyOf.description: Events per second sent on each named output (route/remap outputs); `_default` is the unnamed output.

VersionTelemetry.description: Per-component rates summed across devices verified to be running this exact version (last verified candidate whose digest still matches the managed file) with fresh samples. Rates sum; *_max fields keep the worst device.

device_ids.description: Devices whose fresh samples are included.

coverage.description: Number of fresh device samples that reported each total. Compare with devices_reporting to state partial coverage.

anyOf.description: Events per second sent on each named output (route/remap outputs); `_default` is the unnamed output.

ConfigurationTelemetry.description: The VersionTelemetry aggregate across every version of one pipeline, with a per-version coverage breakdown (newest version first).

rollback_of.description: For a rollback: the deployment it rolled back.

AssignmentDescription.description: Display metadata for an assignment. Names and numbers only: never selectors, targets, variable values or artifacts.

chosen_by_you.description: The request named at least one canary device.

chosen.description: Named by the request rather than picked by the scheduler.

readiness.description: ready: online, healthy and reporting metrics. no_metrics: online and healthy but nothing to measure delivery against. failing: online but failing or not delivering. paused: sync paused. away: not checking in.

CanaryPlan.description: Who a canary rollout releases first, in release order, and why. The scheduler releases exactly these devices as the first stage.

released_early.description: Set on a stage that someone released before the stage ahead of it finished observing or measuring (POST /deployments/{id}/release-next-stage): who, and when. Null otherwise. Omitted by older servers.

state.description: A failed target state, or degraded: applied but an open DATA_PLANE_* issue on this version (message is its title, diagnostic its reason).

fix.description: Degraded groups only: the issue's fix.

code.description: The leading finding's code: the agent diagnostic (ADDRESS_IN_USE, VRL_E100, …) for this exact candidate, or the DATA_PLANE_* issue of a degraded group. A code the pipeline must fix means retrying the same version gives the same result.

component_id.description: The component that finding names, when it names one.

field.description: The field of that component, when the agent reported one.

buffer_utilization.description: Degraded groups: how full that component's buffer was in the first device's latest telemetry sample, when reported. No trend is implied.

device_ids.description: Every device in the group, bounded; devices lists the first few with names.

canary_watch.description: Canary rollouts with a released canary; null otherwise. Omitted by older servers.

RolloutLanes.description: Waves recovered from persisted release times; queued waves follow the scheduler order (pending targets by device ID, canary first, then batches). Failures group current failed targets by diagnostic or error.

window_seconds.description: How far before its release a device's baseline reaches.

gate_reason.description: Why the canary gate is not counting this device as verified right now, by the same predicate that decides whether the rollout may go on; null when it is counted.

now.description: The device's latest sample, or null when it reports no fresh telemetry.

minutes.description: Minutes of stored telemetry the averages cover.

baseline.description: Averages of the stored minute samples before the release, or null when there are none. Never a zero standing in for missing history.

samples.description: Delivery checks on this version so far, against the number the gate needs. Null when the device reports no metrics.

more.description: Canary devices beyond the five listed.

CanaryWatch.description: What the canary devices of a running canary rollout deliver now, beside the same numbers over the minutes before their release, read from telemetry the server already stores. At most five devices, by name.

DeviceListTelemetry.description: The latest device-level sample. Per-component numbers are on GET /api/v1/devices/{id}.

configuration_mode.description: Locally granted capability profile reported by the device; omission means restricted. Never writable through remote policy.

status.description: Computed status. awaiting_first_check_in: enrolled but never checked in. offline: more than three check-in intervals late.

labels.description: Descriptive labels from the enrollment token that enrolled the device (at most 8; lowercase keys, values of 1 to 128 characters without control characters). They never grant group membership, assignments, policy or secret access.

retry_preconditions.description: Retry requires the reviewed desired version and generation plus current retryable state and enabled sync.

desired_sha256.description: Exact rendered artifact digest for the currently released device generation. Version identity, delivered artifact bytes, and actual managed-file digest are distinct.

reported_apply_state.description: Agent-reported workload state, separate from progress of the current desired assignment.

evaluations.description: Evaluations on this version, counted up to the canary measurement count (3 by default; editable under Settings → Notifications → Detection, 1 to 20).

issues.description: The first open issue (stalls first), or none; issue_count counts them all.

issue_count.description: Open issues on this version. List rows (DeviceListItem) carry only the first of them in issues.

data_plane.description: Data-plane health measured from telemetry on the version the device verifiably runs, or, when the device reports no metrics, from sink request failures in its Vector log summary (weaker evidence; evaluations stays 0); absent until the first evaluation. The device reads Not delivering while status is verified, version_id equals desired_version_id and issues is nonempty.

held_on_previous_version.description: Present only, and true, on a device whose status is failed or rolled_back but which verifiably keeps running an earlier version (its managed file still matches the digest the agent verified for it), whose Vector is not reported stopped, and which has no open delivery issue measured on that version. It is held there, not failed: status stays what the agent reported. Absent otherwise, and on older servers.

secret_names.description: Secret names bound on the device, sorted, as its agent last reported them; absent for agents that do not report them. A version needs the names of its vectory-secret:NAME references.

service_manager.description: What keeps the agent running, from enrollment and the latest check-in that reported it; absent for agents that do not report it. none means no service manager keeps it running: after setup's single check-in nothing does until the operator runs it.

vector_running.description: Whether Vector runs on the device, from its latest check-in; absent when the agent does not report it. false with a failed first version means nothing runs.

agent_features.description: What the agent announced it can do in its latest check-in (validation: it can be checked on, see Check on devices); absent when that check-in announced nothing. Names the server does not know are kept as given and never acted on.

readiness.description: Facts the agent reported about the host in its latest check-in: whether its data directory is writable and how many listeners its local capability policy allows (a count, never the list). Absent when that check-in reported none; each member is absent when the agent did not say. Reported, not verified by the server.

agent_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the agent build running on the device, from its latest check-in; absent when the agent does not report it. Compared with the release catalog to say a device already runs a build.

state_dir.description: Where the agent keeps its state on the device, from its latest check-in; absent when the agent does not report it. The deploy dialog puts it in the host commands it writes.

check_in_seconds.description: Current check-in interval; until the agent acknowledges a policy change, the longer of the old and new interval.

running_version.description: Last verified managed version on the host, which keeps running after a failed update or a removed assignment. Null means no managed version was ever verified (the host runs its adopted local config).

DeviceListItem.description: A device as GET /api/v1/devices and the Overview list it: the Device without host_runtime, vector_log_summary and telemetry.components, and with only the first open data-plane issue. GET /api/v1/devices/{id} returns the full Device.

changed.description: true: this device's desired or policy generation differs from the ones the agent sent, its access was revoked, or a check on devices is waiting for it: check in now. false: nothing changed (the hold ended, a newer wait from this device replaced this one, or the server is stopping).

WaitAnswer.description: An unsigned hint, never authority: no configuration, no state change. The agent answers changed:true with an ordinary heartbeat, whose signed manifest is authoritative; a forged or stale answer can only cause an early heartbeat.

retry_after.description: Seconds before the next wait; the same value as Retry-After.

outdated_device_count.description: Applied from this template before its latest edit; they keep the earlier values until it is applied again.

SavedPolicyListItem.description: Applied devices are live devices whose winning settings assignment was applied from this template, or (for assignments made before templates were linked) carries exactly these settings.

name.description: At most 120 UTF-8 bytes. No line breaks, control characters or text-direction overrides, at the ends too: a name that has one is refused with 400 and a sentence that names the field.

rollback_of.description: For a rollback: the deployment it rolled back.

targets.description: group when the assignment's selector names at least one group, otherwise devices. With target_mode persistent a group-targeting assignment follows the group's members; a snapshot was applied to the members it had.

groups.description: At most three of the groups this assignment targets that hold the device. Empty when it targets devices.

assignments.description: The two assignments of the same kind that would both deliver to the device at this priority with different payloads. Told apart by id, never by position.

MembershipConflict.description: One collision a group edit would create. Names and numbers only: never selectors, member lists, payloads or secrets.

details.description: Additive. Present on a 409 CONFLICT that refuses a group edit for conflicting equal-priority assignments (PUT /groups/{id}, POST /groups) and on the matching blocker of a membership preview: at most the first ten collisions, ordered by device name, then device ID. Absent on every other error; older clients ignore it.

details_total.description: How many collisions the edit creates in all; details lists at most ten of them.

GroupMembershipPreview.description: Read-only simulation of a membership edit with the real resolver, rolled back afterwards. pending names a winning assignment that has not released the device yet.

offered_at.description: When the artifact was stored for this generation; null for a generation assigned before artifacts were stored per generation, which is its version's own artifact.

path.description: RFC 6901 pointer to the declared leaf.

value.description: What the offered artifact holds at the declared path. Null when the declared field is a credential field or the value is a secret or a reference to one: those are never shown.

source.description: device: a value set for this device. default: the deployment's default for every device it targets. group is reserved for group-level defaults and is not sent yet. Null when no deployment of this device explains the value, for example a rollback, which binds none.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the managed file as the agent last reported it (its actual_sha256); null when it reports none.

template_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the offered artifact the agent applied, reported only for a version that reads device secrets; null otherwise.

matches.description: true: the agent runs the artifact in this response. false: it reports another digest, a local edit or an activation not finished. null: nothing to compare (no digest reported, nothing offered, or a revoked device, which can no longer report). For a version that reads device secrets the file holds the host's own values and never has the offered digest, so true means the agent applied this template and its file is unchanged since the server verified it.

matches_generation.description: The newest generation this device was offered whose artifact the agent reports running, when that is not the one in this response: by its file digest, or for a version that reads device secrets by the template it applied. Also sent when nothing is offered at the current generation. Null when the report matches this response, when the digest was never offered to this device (the server never sees a local file), or when nothing was reported.

reported_at.description: The device's last check-in (last_seen); null until it has checked in.

generation.description: The generation this response describes: the current desired generation, or the one requested.

current.description: Whether generation is the device's current desired generation.

version.description: The immutable template identity; null when nothing was offered at this generation.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of content, the per-device rendered bytes the device downloads.

format.description: json for what the server renders today, detected from the bytes.

content.description: Exactly the bytes offered, at most 1 MiB. Device secrets are still vectory-secret:NAME references; the server never sees what a host resolves them to.

variables.description: The version's declared variables with the values this device was offered.

previous.description: The newest generation offered before this one; null when there is none. Its bytes can be identical (a retry or a version that only moved nodes).

generations.description: Generations this device was offered, newest first, at most 50 of total.

DeviceConfiguration.description: What a device was offered at its current (or an earlier) desired generation, read from the immutable content-addressed store, with the agent's report beside it. With nothing offered at the current generation (a device never assigned, or its assignment removed) version, sha256, size, format and content are null and previous names the last offer. Revoked devices stay readable as history.

section.description: The components enclosing the first changed line, as dotted keys (sinks.out.buffer); null at the top level or when the text is not the rendered JSON.

from.description: The older side; null when nothing was offered to this device before the newer side.

identical.description: The two sides are the same bytes.

counts.description: Lines of the whole change, not only the part shown. A line a replaced line stands in for counts once, as changed.

unified.description: The same hunks as a unified diff, at most 2,000 lines including its headers; when truncated, its last line is a marker.

truncated.description: The diff is longer than 2,000 lines; hunks and unified stop at the same line.

total_lines.description: Lines the complete unified diff would have.

approximate.description: The change was too large to match line by line, so the region between the unchanged start and end is shown as replaced although some of its lines are the same on both sides.

DeviceConfigurationDiff.description: A bounded comparison of two generations this device was offered, by default the previous one with the current one.

name.description: At most 200 bytes, no control characters.

not_run.description: Vector did not run this test, for example because another test could not be read or built. It never counts as passed. Null is treated as absent.

message.description: At most 512 bytes, no control characters; redacted on the device like a diagnostic. Null is treated as absent.

ValidationTest.description: One of the pipeline's own tests as `vector test` ran it on the device. Reported only when the check asked for tests (run_tests).

id.description: The validation.id of the manifest that asked, exactly as sent (lowercase, hyphenated).

valid.description: The device validated the candidate with its own Vector, local capability policy and device-local secrets, and nothing it found is an error.

diagnostics.description: At most 20 redacted findings, errors first, each at most 512 serialized bytes; the server keeps errors first whatever order they arrive in. Absent or null means none.

tests.description: At most 100. Absent or null means none.

duration_ms.description: How long the device took. Absent or null means not reported.

secrets_missing.description: Names only, sorted, at most 64: the device-secret names the candidate references that this device has not bound. Never file paths or values. Absent or null means none.

ValidationResult.description: The answer of one device to one check, sent in every heartbeat until the manifest it receives no longer carries that validation.id. Strict like every heartbeat member: unknown keys, an oversized list or text, a malformed ID, an answer that serializes to more than 128 KiB as the server stores it, refuse the whole heartbeat with 400 INVALID_INPUT (so an agent must not resend an answer the server refused). An answer for an ID that is unknown, belongs to another device, was already answered or has expired is ignored, never an error. It changes no desired state, generation, policy or issue.

Readiness.description: Facts the agent reported about the host in its latest check-in: whether its data directory is writable and how many listeners its local capability policy allows (a count, never the list). Absent when that check-in reported none; each member is absent when the agent did not say. Reported, not verified by the server.

id.description: The check this device answers. Every device of one request shares it; with the device it identifies the row.

sha256.description: Digest of the candidate this device is asked to validate: the artifact the review computed for it, with its own variable values applied and device secrets still vectory-secret:NAME references.

artifact_path.description: Always the path of sha256. Only this device can fetch it, and only while the check is pending and unexpired.

run_tests.description: Also run the pipeline's own tests (vector test).

expires_at.description: UTC, ten minutes after the check was requested.

request_id.description: Optional durable create identity scoped to the authenticated actor. Reuse only with the identical payload.

name.description: Optional; at most 120 characters. No line breaks, control characters or text-direction overrides, at the ends too: a name that has one is refused with 400 and a sentence that names the field.

replaces.description: Existing assignments of the same resource that this deployment explicitly replaces on the selected devices. Until this deployment releases a device the replaced assignment keeps it; each release retires the replaced assignment there (history kept, persistent selectors exclude the device). An assignment left with nothing to deliver is retired (status unassigned, status_before_removal kept). Without replaces, equal-priority different payloads still conflict. A replaced assignment that changed or no longer selects any of these devices returns 409 REPLACEMENT_CHANGED.

policy_id.description: Saved agent settings a policy deployment applies. The policy must equal their current values, otherwise preview and creation return 409.

device_validation.description: Also ask every reviewed device that is not revoked, the first 50 by name, to validate this version on its own host. Needs a pipeline version (not agent settings). Creating a deployment refuses this field.

run_tests.description: With device_validation: also run the pipeline's own tests on each device. Stored with the check; it does nothing on its own.

PreviewRequest.description: A deployment request, previewed. device_validation and run_tests are removed before the request is checked as a deployment, so POST /deployments still refuses them.

name.description: The device's name when the check was requested.

state.description: pending: asked, not answered yet. passed: the device validated the candidate and found no error. failed: it found at least one (diagnostics, tests or secrets_missing say what). offline: it had not checked in for three of its own intervals (or never) when the check was requested, so it was not asked. expired: it did not answer in ten minutes, or a newer check for it replaced this one, or it was revoked. unsupported: it was online but had not announced validation in agent_features, so it was not asked (an older agent).

updated_at.description: When this device last changed state: the request, the answer, the supersede or revocation, or the expiry.

state.description: running while any device is pending; complete otherwise (also once every pending device has expired).

truncated.description: More devices were reviewed than were addressed.

devices.description: In name order (digits compare by value: edge-2 before edge-10).

DeviceValidation.description: What the devices of one preview answered when asked to validate a candidate version on their own hosts. Advisory: no deployment, desired state, generation, policy or issue changes because of an answer, and nothing waits for one. Diagnostics are redacted on the device; the server stores what it received within its bounds and keeps rows 24 hours.

DeviceInventoryCounts.description: Devices matching q, group, version, desired_version and running_version (every filter but status and view), by status and by view, so each chip can show what picking it would list. status buckets are the Devices page's: applied (verified), degraded (applied but not delivering), held (its newest version failed; it still runs an earlier one and delivers on it, see Device.held_on_previous_version), updating (applying), check (verification_unknown), failed (failed, rolled_back, conflict), offline (offline, awaiting_first_check_in), paused (paused, pause_requested), unmanaged; a state added later counts as updating. Views never count revoked devices.

device_groups.description: Each row's groups by name (at most 10) and how many there are, keyed by device ID.

DeviceInventoryPage.description: One page of devices exactly as GET /api/v1/devices lists them. Filtering, order and counts come from a fleet projection at most 2 seconds old that any change through the dashboard API replaces; the rows are read when the page is.

truncated.description: More than 10,000 devices match; ids holds the first 10,000 in order.

name.description: Null for a member the fleet projection does not know (status unavailable).

status.description: The state the device's badge shows: its status, degraded while applied but not delivering, held while its newest version failed and it keeps running an earlier one, pause_requested until the agent acknowledges a pause, or unavailable.

GroupSummary.description: A group list row with slim=1: the Group without device_ids.

connection.description: never: enrolled but never checked in.

waiting_device.description: The first device by name that never checked in.

telemetry.description: From each non-revoked device's latest sample when it is at most 3 minutes old (reporting); stale samples are older. A total no fresh device reported is null, never zero. errors sums counters since each Vector started. disabled counts devices without a fresh sample whose settings turn metrics off.

OverviewCounts.description: What the dashboard used to derive from every device: devices by health bucket (see DeviceInventoryCounts), by connection, and fleet throughput.

cause.description: Most urgent first: not delivering, failed, rolled back, check required, held on the previous version, offline.

reason.description: degraded: the open issue's measured reason. failed and rolled_back: the sanitized failure summary.

since.description: degraded: when the issue opened; offline: the last check-in.

phase.description: observing: every released device verified and the observation window runs. measuring: a released device's delivery is still being measured. waiting: released devices are still verifying.

devices_reporting.description: Of those, devices with a sample at most 3 minutes old.

groups.description: The groups holding most of these devices, and how many of them each holds.

not_delivering.description: Devices applied on this version with an open delivery issue.

canary.description: The newest active canary rollout of this version.

OverviewRunning.description: One pipeline version that live devices verifiably run as they last reported it (the last verified version whose digest still matches the managed file), not what is desired. Rates sum fresh samples (at most 3 minutes old); null when none reported. state: not_delivering when a device is, else canary during an active canary rollout, else running.

offline_minutes.description: device.offline goes out once an outage lasts this long, measured from the last check-in; a device is offline after three missed check-ins.

pipeline_ids.description: Only events about these pipelines. Empty means every pipeline.

group_ids.description: Only events about devices in these groups (for rollouts: its selector groups and its targets' groups). Empty means every group.

errors_bypass.description: Error-severity problems go out during quiet hours; recoveries and warnings wait.

NotificationRules.description: What a channel sends. Messages held by quiet hours go out as one digest when they end.

allow_private.description: Allows private, CGNAT, unique local and loopback addresses (and plain http:// to them). Link-local, multicast, reserved and cloud metadata addresses are never contacted.

url_hint.description: The saved URL's origin; its path and query are write-only.

security.description: starttls upgrades a plain connection and refuses a server that can't; tls encrypts from the first byte (port 465); none only reaches a relay on the server's own loopback address, with allow_private.

secrets_readable.description: False when the saved secrets can't be opened with this instance's keys (restored without them); replace them.

NotificationChannel.description: Secrets (the webhook URL's path and query, signing secret, header value and SMTP password) are write-only: responses carry only whether each is set.

url.description: https:// (http:// only with allow_private). No user name or password. Write-only: omit on update to keep the saved URL.

anyOf.description: Write-only. Omit to keep; null or empty removes it.
Write-only, printable ASCII. Omit to keep; null or empty removes it.

security.description: starttls upgrades a plain connection and refuses a server that can't; tls encrypts from the first byte (port 465); none only reaches a relay on the server's own loopback address, with allow_private.

anyOf.description: Write-only. Omit to keep; null or empty removes it.

revision.description: Required on update, where a stale value returns 409 STALE_REVISION; absent on create.

id.description: Stable per event (and per test or digest): receivers can drop a repeat. A restart during a send can deliver a message twice.

url.description: A dashboard link when VECTORY_PUBLIC_URL is set.

restored.description: Only on rollout.rolled_back: the pipeline version the rollback restored, or null when that is not known. It can belong to another pipeline than the rolled-back deployment.

count.description: Digests only: how many notifications it summarises.

NotificationEvent.description: The machine-readable event in every webhook body, beside Slack's text and blocks. Headers: X-Vectory-Event (type), X-Vectory-Delivery (delivery ID) and, with a signing secret, X-Vectory-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">.

status_code.description: HTTP status, or the SMTP reply code.

outcome.description: retrying: failed, next attempt at next_attempt_at. failed: refused in a way a retry won't fix (address policy, a 4xx other than 408, 425 and 429). gave_up: the fourth attempt failed.

error.description: Bounded; secrets, URL paths and receiver echoes of them are redacted.

DetectionThresholds.description: The editable part of data-plane detection (see Data-plane health). Defaults equal the evaluator's constants.
